# react-native-whats-new

> A paged "what's new" bottom sheet for React Native and Expo, shown automatically on the first launch after an app update, optionally followed by the native App Store / Play Store rating prompt. Pure JS: no native code, no config plugin, works in Expo Go, iOS and Android.

This file is the complete integration guide for coding agents. Everything below matches the published TypeScript API; do not invent props that are not listed here.

## What it does

- You keep a list of releases (`notes`), each a version string plus one or more pages.
- On every mount it compares the app's marketing version (`currentVersion`) with the last version it stored in `storage`.
- On the first launch after an update where `notes` has a release for the new version, it slides up a paged sheet. When the user closes it (tapping "Got it" on the last page, swiping it down, tapping the backdrop, or Android back), that version is stored as seen.
- If `requestReview` is passed, it is called after the user taps "Got it" and the sheet has finished animating out.
- A fresh install never shows anything: it silently stores the current version, so the next update is the first one to show.

## Install

Expo (managed or dev build):

```sh
npx expo install react-native-whats-new @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
# version source + rating prompt (optional, both work in Expo Go)
npx expo install expo-application expo-store-review
```

Bare React Native (use the project's package manager: npm, yarn, pnpm or bun):

```sh
npm install react-native-whats-new @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
# version source + rating prompt (optional)
npm install react-native-device-info react-native-in-app-review
cd ios && pod install
```

`react-native-whats-new` itself has no native code; `pod install` is only for the native peers (AsyncStorage, device-info, in-app-review). Peer deps: `react >= 18`, `react-native >= 0.72`. It does not need reanimated, gesture-handler or safe-area-context.

If the app already uses MMKV or another key-value store, reuse it through an adapter (see Storage) instead of adding AsyncStorage.

## Where the inputs come from

- `currentVersion`: the MARKETING version ("1.4.0" = CFBundleShortVersionString / versionName), never the build number.
  - Expo: `Application.nativeApplicationVersion` from `expo-application` (a `string | null`).
  - Bare: `getVersion()` from `react-native-device-info`.
  - In development these return the native binary's version (Expo Go reports Expo Go's own version); to test, pass a literal like `'1.4.0'`.
- `requestReview`:
  - Expo: `() => StoreReview.requestReview()` from `expo-store-review`.
  - Bare: `() => InAppReview.RequestInAppReview()` from `react-native-in-app-review`.
- `storage`: `AsyncStorage` from `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage`, or an adapter.

## Storage

Required. Any object with this shape (sync or async):

```ts
type WhatsNewStorage = {
  getItem(key: string): Promise<string | null> | string | null | undefined;
  setItem(key: string, value: string): Promise<void> | void;
};
```

`storage={AsyncStorage}` fits directly. MMKV does NOT (it has `getString`/`set`), so wrap it:

```ts
import { MMKV } from 'react-native-mmkv';

const mmkv = new MMKV();
export const whatsNewStorage = {
  getItem: (key: string) => mmkv.getString(key) ?? null,
  setItem: (key: string, value: string) => mmkv.set(key, value),
};
```

The library uses one key: `react-native-whats-new:last-seen-version`. Storage failures never throw into the app: a failed read means "don't show this launch".

## Notes and page types

```ts
type WhatsNewRelease = { version: string; pages: WhatsNewPage[] };

type WhatsNewPage =
  | { type: 'list'; title: string; rows: WhatsNewListRow[] }
  | {
      type: 'media';
      kind: 'image' | 'video';
      source: { uri: string } | number; // remote, or require('./x.png')
      poster?: { uri: string } | number; // shown for video without renderVideo
      aspectRatio?: number; // width ÷ height, default 1 (square, cropped); 3 / 4 shows a portrait photo whole
      title?: string;
      description?: string;
    }
  | { type: 'custom'; render: () => ReactNode };

type WhatsNewListRow = {
  icon?: ReactNode | ImageSourcePropType; // an emoji string, your icon element, or an image
  title: string;
  description?: string;
};
```

- Versions are semver-ish: "1.2.0" and "1.2" are equal; "-beta" / "+7" suffixes are ignored.
- One release per version. A release with zero pages never shows.
- Video pages only play if you pass `renderVideo`; otherwise they show `poster`.
- `custom` pages are functions, so they cannot come from remote JSON.

## `<WhatsNew />` props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notes` | `readonly WhatsNewRelease[] \| null` | required | Inline array literals are fine (compared by content). `null` = still loading |
| `currentVersion` | `string \| null \| undefined` | required | `null`/`undefined` = wait, check nothing yet |
| `storage` | `WhatsNewStorage` | required | AsyncStorage or an adapter |
| `matchMode` | `'exact' \| 'minor'` | `'exact'` | `'minor'`: 1.2.3 reuses the newest 1.2.x notes not newer than the app |
| `showOnFirstInstall` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `when` | `() => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | none | App gate; `false` or a throw = skip this launch, nothing marked seen |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` = no storage reads/writes, no show; evaluates when it turns `true` |
| `onEvent` | `(event: WhatsNewEvent) => void` | none | Throws are swallowed |
| `requestReview` | `() => Promise<unknown> \| unknown` | none | Omit for notes-only |
| `reviewOn` | `'done' \| 'done-or-dismiss' \| 'never'` | `'done'` | `'never'` = notes-only even with `requestReview` |
| `reviewDelayMs` | `number` | `400` | Counted from the end of the sheet's out-animation |
| `theme` | `Partial<WhatsNewTheme>` | system light/dark | Merged over `defaultTheme` / `darkTheme` |
| `labels` | `Partial<WhatsNewLabels>` | English | For localization |
| `sheetHeight` | `'standard' \| 'full'` | `'standard'` | standard = content-sized, max 75% of the window |
| `renderVideo` | `(source, page) => ReactNode` | none | e.g. an expo-video `VideoView` |
| `insets` | `{ top: number; bottom: number }` | `{ top: 0, bottom: 0 }` | Pass `useSafeAreaInsets()`; the sheet adds 24px |
| `ref` | `Ref<WhatsNewHandle>` | none | `ref.current?.show(version): boolean` |

```ts
type WhatsNewTheme = {
  background: string; text: string; secondaryText: string;
  accent: string; onAccent: string; dot: string; backdrop: string;
  radius: number;
  fonts: { title?: string; body?: string; button?: string }; // families, no weights
};
type WhatsNewLabels = {
  next: string; // 'Continue'
  done: string; // 'Got it'
  close: string; // 'Close' (accessibility label)
  page: (index: number, count: number) => string; // 'Page 1 of 3', 1-based
};
type WhatsNewEvent =
  | { type: 'shown'; version: string; pageCount: number; manual: boolean }
  | { type: 'page_viewed'; version: string; pageIndex: number; pageCount: number }
  | { type: 'done'; version: string; pageIndex: number; pageCount: number }
  | { type: 'dismissed'; version: string; pageIndex: number; pageCount: number }
  | { type: 'review_requested'; version: string };
```

Events carry shapes only (versions, indices, counts, booleans), never note text.

## When it shows

Checked once per mount (again if `currentVersion`, `matchMode`, `showOnFirstInstall`, the notes' content, or `enabled` change):

1. `enabled` is false or `currentVersion` is null/undefined: nothing, no storage access.
2. No stored version (fresh install, or first release that includes this library): nothing shown; current version stored. `showOnFirstInstall` overrides.
3. Current version <= stored version (same version, downgrade, or unparseable order): nothing.
4. Update, but `notes` has no release for it (or it has zero pages): nothing; current version stored, so notes added later for this version never show.
5. Update with a matching release: `when()` is awaited if given (false = retry next launch), then the sheet shows. Only the current version's notes show; skipped versions are not replayed.
6. Closing the automatic sheet (any way) stores the version as seen.

Manual shows via `ref.current?.show(version)` (exact version match) never touch storage and never ask for a review. They return `false` when that version has no notes.

Rating: asked only after an automatic show, when the user tapped "Got it" on the last page (`reviewOn='done'`) or also on any dismissal (`'done-or-dismiss'`), after `reviewDelayMs`. Emits `review_requested` just before calling `requestReview`. A throwing or rejecting `requestReview` is swallowed.

## Canonical integration: Expo Router

`constants/whatsNew.ts` (or `whatsNew.ts`):

```ts
import type { WhatsNewRelease } from 'react-native-whats-new';

export const whatsNewNotes: WhatsNewRelease[] = [
  {
    version: '1.4.0', // the version in app.json / app.config "version"
    pages: [
      {
        type: 'list',
        title: "What's new",
        rows: [
          { icon: '⚡️', title: 'Faster sync', description: 'Changes land in under a second.' },
          { icon: '🌙', title: 'Dark mode', description: 'Follows your system setting.' },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
];
```

`app/_layout.tsx`:

```tsx
import { Stack } from 'expo-router';
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import * as Application from 'expo-application';
import * as StoreReview from 'expo-store-review';
import { useSafeAreaInsets } from 'react-native-safe-area-context';
import { WhatsNew } from 'react-native-whats-new';
import { whatsNewNotes } from '../constants/whatsNew';

export default function RootLayout() {
  const insets = useSafeAreaInsets(); // Expo Router provides SafeAreaProvider
  return (
    <>
      <Stack />
      <WhatsNew
        notes={whatsNewNotes}
        currentVersion={Application.nativeApplicationVersion}
        storage={AsyncStorage}
        insets={insets}
        requestReview={() => StoreReview.requestReview()}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

Keep the app's existing providers and navigator; add `<WhatsNew />` as a sibling of the navigator inside them. It renders a `Modal`, so its position in the tree does not matter, only that it stays mounted.

## Canonical integration: bare React Native

`App.tsx`:

```tsx
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import { getVersion } from 'react-native-device-info';
import InAppReview from 'react-native-in-app-review';
import { SafeAreaProvider, useSafeAreaInsets } from 'react-native-safe-area-context';
import { WhatsNew } from 'react-native-whats-new';
import { whatsNewNotes } from './whatsNew';
import { RootNavigator } from './navigation';

function Root() {
  const insets = useSafeAreaInsets();
  return (
    <>
      <RootNavigator />
      <WhatsNew
        notes={whatsNewNotes}
        currentVersion={getVersion()}
        storage={AsyncStorage}
        insets={insets}
        requestReview={() => InAppReview.RequestInAppReview()}
      />
    </>
  );
}

export default function App() {
  return (
    <SafeAreaProvider>
      <Root />
    </SafeAreaProvider>
  );
}
```

Without safe-area-context, drop `insets`.

## Onboarding, auth and remote notes

```tsx
<WhatsNew enabled={hasFinishedOnboarding} /* ... */ />
```

- `enabled={false}` while onboarding, sign-in or a paywall is on screen, so the sheet never covers it; it evaluates as soon as `enabled` becomes true.
- `markWhatsNewSeen(storage, version)` at the end of onboarding stores the current version without showing anything (needed with `showOnFirstInstall`, or if the component could evaluate before onboarding ends).
- `when={() => ...}` for an async gate (e.g. "not during a call"); false retries next launch.
- Remote notes: pass `notes={null}` until they have loaded and passed `validateNotes`. `null` means "still loading": nothing is evaluated or stored. An empty array means "no notes", and the version is stored as seen.

## Settings row ("What's new")

```tsx
import { createRef } from 'react';
import { Pressable, Text } from 'react-native';
import * as Application from 'expo-application';
import type { WhatsNewHandle } from 'react-native-whats-new';

// Shared ref: pass it as <WhatsNew ref={whatsNewRef} /> at the root.
export const whatsNewRef = createRef<WhatsNewHandle>();

export function WhatsNewRow() {
  return (
    <Pressable
      onPress={() =>
        whatsNewRef.current?.show(Application.nativeApplicationVersion ?? '')
      }
    >
      <Text>What's new</Text>
    </Pressable>
  );
}
```

## Headless hook

```tsx
import { useWhatsNew, WhatsNewSheet } from 'react-native-whats-new';

const wn = useWhatsNew({ notes, currentVersion, storage: AsyncStorage });
<WhatsNewSheet
  release={wn.release}
  visible={wn.visible}
  onClose={(via, pageIndex) => wn.close(via, pageIndex)}
  onPageChange={wn.reportPage}
/>;
```

`useWhatsNew(options)` takes `notes, currentVersion, storage, matchMode, showOnFirstInstall, when, enabled, onEvent` and returns `{ visible: boolean; release: WhatsNewRelease | null; manual: boolean; show(version): boolean; close(via: 'done' | 'dismissed', pageIndex): void; reportPage(pageIndex): void }`. The hook never asks for a review; call your review API yourself after `close('done', ...)`.

`WhatsNewSheet` props: `release, visible, onClose(via, pageIndex), onPageChange?, onHidden?, theme?, labels?, sheetHeight?, renderVideo?, insets?`.

## Helpers

- `markWhatsNewSeen(storage, version): Promise<void>`: store a version as seen without showing.
- `resetWhatsNew(storage): Promise<void>`: forget the seen version (next launch = fresh install). Dev only.
- `validateNotes(json: unknown)`: `{ ok: true; notes } | { ok: false; errors: string[] }` for notes from remote JSON (`list` and `media` only; icons/sources must be `{ uri }`).
- `compareVersions(a, b): number | null`: -1 / 0 / 1, `null` when unparseable and different.
- `defaultTheme`, `darkTheme`, `defaultLabels`.

## Seeing it in development

A fresh install is silent by design. To see the sheet:

1. Pass a literal older version, reload, then the newer one: `currentVersion="1.3.0"` then `"1.4.0"` with notes for 1.4.0; or
2. `await markWhatsNewSeen(AsyncStorage, '0.0.0')` once, then reload; or
3. Temporarily `showOnFirstInstall` after `resetWhatsNew(AsyncStorage)`.

In `__DEV__` the library warns (`[react-native-whats-new] ...`) about a storage without getItem/setItem, a `currentVersion` that is not a marketing version, and duplicate versions in `notes`.

## Common mistakes

- Passing an MMKV instance as `storage`. MMKV has `getString`/`set`, not `getItem`/`setItem`; use the adapter above.
- Using the build number (`nativeBuildVersion`, `getBuildNumber()`, "42") as `currentVersion`. Use the marketing version.
- Mounting `<WhatsNew />` inside a screen that unmounts (a tab, a modal route). Mount it once at the root.
- Expecting it on first install. Fresh installs are silent; only updates show notes.
- Mounting it during onboarding or sign-in without `enabled={false}` (and `markWhatsNewSeen` when onboarding ends if you use `showOnFirstInstall`).
- Adding a "Do you like the app?" pre-question before `requestReview`. Google Play policy forbids any question before the review prompt; call it directly.
- Testing the rating prompt in TestFlight (iOS never shows it there; it shows in dev builds and App Store installs, max 3 times per 365 days) or from a sideloaded Android APK / `expo start` (Play shows it only for Play-installed builds, including internal testing, with an undisclosed quota). `requestReview` never tells you whether it showed.
- Putting `custom` pages in remote JSON. They are functions; remote notes are `list` and `media` only, checked with `validateNotes`.
- Passing `[]` while remote notes load: an empty array is a real answer ("no notes"), so the version gets stored as seen before they arrive. Pass `null` while loading.
- Two releases with the same version (or "1.2" and "1.2.0"): only the first is used.
